   102	}
   103	
   104	/** The refusal itself, so every path that refuses says the same thing. */
   105	export function reconciledLockedError(): ConflictException {
   106	  return new ConflictException(
   107	    tr(
   108	      "errors.transactions.reconciledLocked",
   109	      "This transaction is reconciled and locked. Turn off 'Lock reconciled transactions' in Settings to change it.",
   110	    ),
   111	  );
   112	}
   113	
   114	/** Read the effective user's strict-lock preference inside the caller's transaction. */
   115	export async function isReconciledLockEnabled(
   116	  manager: EntityManager,
   117	  userId: string,
   118	): Promise<boolean> {
   119	  const prefs = await manager.getRepository(UserPreference).findOne({
   120	    where: { userId },
   121	    select: { userId: true, lockReconciledTransactions: true },
   122	  });

   124	}
   125	
   126	/** The subset of a locked transaction row this guard reads. */
   127	export interface ReconciledLockCandidate {
   128	  readonly status: string | null;
   129	}
   130	
   131	/** What a caller may ask the lock to make an exception for. */
   132	export interface ReconciledLockOptions {
   133	  /**
   134	   * The id of the single row being changed, when the caller is performing a
   135	   * **status transition** and wants the undo window of
   136	   * `RECONCILED_UNDO_WINDOW_SECONDS` honoured.
   137	   *
   138	   * Passing it means the assertion returns rather than throwing for a row that
   139	   * became reconciled moments ago -- so the caller then **must** refuse
   140	   * anything that is not an undo (`isReconciledUndo`) itself, because at that
   141	   * point only the caller knows which transition it is about to make.
   142	   * `reconciled-lock.guard.spec.ts` fails on a call site that asks for the
   143	   * window and does not.
   144	   */
   145	  undoWindowFor?: string;
   146	}
   147	
   148	/** What the assertion learned, for a caller that opened the undo window. */
   149	export interface ReconciledLockVerdict {
   150	  /**
   151	   * True when the row is locked *and* fresh enough to be taken back -- the one
   152	   * state in which the caller is responsible for the second half of the rule.
   153	   * False whenever the lock did not apply at all, so it can never be read as
   154	   * "the lock is off".
   155	   */
   156	  undoWindowOpen: boolean;
   157	}
   158	
   159	/**
   160	 * Refuse the caller's write when any of `rows` is RECONCILED and the effective
   161	 * user has the strict lock on.
   162	 *
   163	 * Call it inside the mutation's `withScopedDb` callback, after the rows are
   164	 * locked and before anything is written. A row that is not reconciled costs
   165	 * nothing: the preference is read only when at least one candidate is
   166	 * RECONCILED.
   167	 */
   168	export async function assertReconciledRowsMutable(
   169	  manager: EntityManager,
   170	  userId: string,
   171	  rows: readonly ReconciledLockCandidate[],
   172	  options: ReconciledLockOptions = {},
   173	): Promise<ReconciledLockVerdict> {
   174	  const closed = { undoWindowOpen: false };
   175	  const hasReconciled = rows.some(
   176	    (row) => row?.status === TransactionStatus.RECONCILED,
   177	  );
   178	  if (!hasReconciled) return closed;
   179	  if (!(await isReconciledLockEnabled(manager, userId))) return closed;

   181	  if (
   182	    options.undoWindowFor &&
   183	    (await isWithinReconciledUndoWindow(manager, options.undoWindowFor))
   184	  ) {
   185	    return { undoWindowOpen: true };
   186	  }
   187	
   188	  throw reconciledLockedError();
   189	}
   190	
   191	/**
   192	 * The id-list form, for a batch that does not hydrate every row it writes.
   193	 *
   194	 * Runs the same refusal as `assertReconciledRowsMutable` from a single
   195	 * `SELECT`, so a bulk update or bulk delete cannot be the one door into a
   196	 * locked row. Call it inside the batch's transaction, before its first write.
   197	 */
   198	export async function assertReconciledIdsMutable(
   199	  manager: EntityManager,
   200	  userId: string,
   201	  ids: readonly string[],
   202	): Promise<void> {
   203	  if (ids.length === 0) return;
   204	  const rows: { status: string | null }[] = await manager.query(
   205	    `SELECT status FROM transactions
   206	      WHERE id = ANY($1::uuid[]) AND user_id = $2 AND status = $3
   207	      LIMIT 1`,
   208	    [[...new Set(ids)], userId, TransactionStatus.RECONCILED],
   209	  );

   211	}

1	import { EntityManager } from "typeorm";
     2	import { ScheduledTransaction } from "./entities/scheduled-transaction.entity";
     3	import { ScheduledTransactionOverride } from "./entities/scheduled-transaction-override.entity";
     4	import {
     5	  anchorDayOf,
     6	  calculateNextDueDate,
     7	  ensureYMD,
     8	} from "../common/recurrence";
     9	import { todayYMD } from "../common/date-utils";
    10	import { returnedRows } from "../common/db/query-result";
    11	
    12	/** The cursor columns `advanceScheduleCursor` wrote. */
    13	export interface ScheduleCursorAdvance {
    14	  nextDueDate: string;
    15	  occurrencesRemaining: number | null;
    16	  /** True when the advance deactivated the schedule. */
    17	  deactivated: boolean;
    18	  /** How many slots the cursor stepped over, the claimed one included. */
    19	  slotsConsumed: number;
    20	}
    21	
    22	/**
    23	 * Advance a recurring schedule's cursor past the occurrences that have been
    24	 * consumed: `next_due_date` to the next unclaimed slot, overrides dated before
    25	 * it pruned, `last_posted_date` set, `occurrences_remaining` decremented once
    26	 * per slot and the schedule deactivated at zero or past `end_date`.
    27	 *
    28	 * Lifted out of `ScheduledTransactionsService.post()`, so the settlement of a
    29	 * bank debit against an occurrence (`docs/specs/loan-installment-settlement.md`
    30	 * section 12.3) advances the cursor through the same code when it claims the
    31	 * due slot. `post()`, `skip()` and the settlement claim all pass the slot they
    32	 * consume plus every claim on or after it (`claimedSlotsFrom`), so a slot a
    33	 * settlement rule claimed ahead of the cursor is never left under it (audit
    34	 * A26-S08-03).
    35	 *
    36	 * `schedule` is the LOCKED row (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`), never a snapshot
    37	 * taken before the transaction: a concurrent edit to `occurrences_remaining`
    38	 * or `end_date` would otherwise be reverted by this advancement.
    39	 * `consumedSlots` holds the slot dates (YYYY-MM-DD) already claimed on the
    40	 * schedule, the row's current `next_due_date` among them; the cursor steps
    41	 * past every consecutive claimed slot so the bill never offers an occurrence
    42	 * whose own claim key is taken. With exactly the current slot in the set, this
    43	 * is one step.
    44	 *
    45	 * `options.stampLastPosted` (default true) sets `last_posted_date`; a skip
    46	 * passes false because nothing was posted.
    47	 *
    48	 * A ONCE schedule has no next slot; `post()` deletes it instead and never
    49	 * calls this.
    50	 */
    51	export async function advanceScheduleCursor(
    52	  m: EntityManager,
    53	  schedule: Pick<
    54	    ScheduledTransaction,
    55	    "id" | "nextDueDate" | "frequency" | "occurrencesRemaining" | "endDate"
    56	  > &
    57	    Partial<Pick<ScheduledTransaction, "startDate">>,
    58	  consumedSlots: ReadonlySet<string>,
    59	  options: { stampLastPosted?: boolean } = {},
    60	): Promise<ScheduleCursorAdvance> {
    61	  let newNextDueDateStr = ensureYMD(schedule.nextDueDate);
    62	  let slotsConsumed = 0;
    63	  do {
    64	    // `calculateNextDueDate` hands back its input for ONCE and for a value
    65	    // outside `FrequencyType` (the column is a bare VARCHAR), and the current
    66	    // slot is always in the set, so a step that does not advance would loop
    67	    // for ever under the parent lock. Fail closed: the caller's transaction
    68	    // rolls back and nothing is claimed on a schedule whose cadence cannot
    69	    // step.
    70	    const previous = newNextDueDateStr;
    71	    newNextDueDateStr = calculateNextDueDate(
    72	      previous,
    73	      schedule.frequency,
    74	      anchorDayOf(schedule.startDate, previous),
    75	    );
    76	    if (newNextDueDateStr <= previous) {
    77	      throw new Error(
    78	        `advanceScheduleCursor: frequency "${schedule.frequency}" of scheduled ` +
    79	          `transaction ${schedule.id} does not advance ${previous}`,
    80	      );
    81	    }
    82	    slotsConsumed += 1;
    83	  } while (consumedSlots.has(newNextDueDateStr));
    84	
    85	  await m
    86	    .createQueryBuilder()
    87	    .delete()
    88	    .from(ScheduledTransactionOverride)
    89	    .where("scheduledTransactionId = :id", { id: schedule.id })
    90	    .andWhere("originalDate < :newNextDueDate", {
    91	      newNextDueDate: newNextDueDateStr,
    92	    })
    93	    .execute();
    94	
    95	  const updateFields: Partial<ScheduledTransaction> = {
    96	    nextDueDate: newNextDueDateStr,
    97	  };
    98	  if (options.stampLastPosted !== false) {
    99	    updateFields.lastPostedDate = todayYMD();
   100	  }
   101	
   102	  let occurrencesRemaining = schedule.occurrencesRemaining;
   103	  if (
   104	    schedule.occurrencesRemaining !== null &&
   105	    schedule.occurrencesRemaining > 0
   106	  ) {
   107	    occurrencesRemaining = Math.max(
   108	      0,
   109	      schedule.occurrencesRemaining - slotsConsumed,
   110	    );
   111	    updateFields.occurrencesRemaining = occurrencesRemaining;
   112	    if (occurrencesRemaining === 0) {
   113	      updateFields.isActive = false;
   114	    }
   115	  }
   116	
   117	  if (schedule.endDate && newNextDueDateStr > ensureYMD(schedule.endDate)) {
   118	    updateFields.isActive = false;
   119	  }
   120	
   121	  await m.update(ScheduledTransaction, schedule.id, updateFields);
   122	  return {
   123	    nextDueDate: newNextDueDateStr,
   124	    occurrencesRemaining,
   125	    deactivated: updateFields.isActive === false,
   126	    slotsConsumed,
   127	  };
   128	}
   129	
   130	/**
   131	 * The slot dates (YYYY-MM-DD) of every claim on the schedule dated on or after
   132	 * `fromYmd`: the occurrences a post or a settlement rule has already consumed at
   133	 * or ahead of the cursor. Read inside the transaction that holds the schedule
   134	 * lock, after any claim it inserted, so the set passed to
   135	 * `advanceScheduleCursor` is complete.
   136	 */
   137	export async function claimedSlotsFrom(
   138	  m: EntityManager,
   139	  scheduleId: string,
   140	  fromYmd: string,
   141	): Promise<Set<string>> {
   142	  const rows = returnedRows<{ d: string }>(
   143	    await m.query(
   144	      `SELECT TO_CHAR(original_due_date, 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS d
   145	         FROM scheduled_transaction_postings
   146	        WHERE scheduled_transaction_id = $1 AND original_due_date >= $2`,
   147	      [scheduleId, fromYmd],
   148	    ),
   149	  );
   150	  return new Set(rows.map((row) => row.d));
   151	}
   152	
   153	/** The cursor columns of a schedule, as they stand before an advance or after it. */
   154	export interface ScheduleCursorState {
   155	  readonly nextDueDate: string;
   156	  readonly occurrencesRemaining: number | null;
   157	  readonly isActive: boolean;
   158	  readonly lastPostedDate: string | null;
   159	}
   160	
   161	/**
   162	 * An override row an advance pruned, in the shape it is re-inserted in: the
   163	 * entity's own columns, without the timestamps the database regenerates.
   164	 */
   165	export type PrunedScheduleOverride = Pick<
   166	  ScheduledTransactionOverride,
   167	  | "id"
   168	  | "scheduledTransactionId"
   169	  | "originalDate"
   170	  | "overrideDate"
   171	  | "amount"
   172	  | "categoryId"
   173	  | "description"
   174	  | "isSplit"
   175	  | "splits"
   176	  | "investmentQuantity"
   177	  | "investmentPrice"
   178	  | "investmentTotalAmount"
   179	>;
   180	
   181	/**
   182	 * One advance of a schedule's cursor, recorded so it can be undone
   183	 * (`docs/specs/loan-installment-settlement.md` sections 12.4 and 12.6): the
   184	 * cursor columns before and after, and the override rows the advance pruned.
   185	 */
   186	export interface ScheduleCursorChange {
   187	  readonly before: ScheduleCursorState;
   188	  readonly after: ScheduleCursorState;
   189	  readonly prunedOverrides: readonly PrunedScheduleOverride[];
   190	}
   191	
   192	/** The cursor columns of a schedule row as `YYYY-MM-DD` strings and plain values. */
   193	export function scheduleCursorState(
   194	  schedule: Pick<
   195	    ScheduledTransaction,
   196	    "nextDueDate" | "occurrencesRemaining" | "isActive" | "lastPostedDate"
   197	  >,
   198	): ScheduleCursorState {
   199	  return {
   200	    nextDueDate: ensureYMD(schedule.nextDueDate),
   201	    occurrencesRemaining: schedule.occurrencesRemaining ?? null,
   202	    isActive: schedule.isActive,
   203	    lastPostedDate:
   204	      schedule.lastPostedDate === null || schedule.lastPostedDate === undefined
   205	        ? null
   206	        : ensureYMD(schedule.lastPostedDate),
   207	  };
   208	}
   209	
   210	/** The columns of an override row the rewind puts back. */
   211	export function prunedScheduleOverride(
   212	  override: ScheduledTransactionOverride,
   213	): PrunedScheduleOverride {
   214	  return {
   215	    id: override.id,
   216	    scheduledTransactionId: override.scheduledTransactionId,
   217	    originalDate: ensureYMD(override.originalDate),
   218	    overrideDate: ensureYMD(override.overrideDate),
   219	    amount: override.amount ?? null,
   220	    categoryId: override.categoryId ?? null,
   221	    description: override.description ?? null,
   222	    isSplit: override.isSplit ?? null,
   223	    splits: override.splits ?? null,
   224	    investmentQuantity: override.investmentQuantity ?? null,
   225	    investmentPrice: override.investmentPrice ?? null,
   226	    investmentTotalAmount: override.investmentTotalAmount ?? null,
   227	  };
   228	}
   229	
   230	/**
   231	 * The inverse of one `advanceScheduleCursor`, for the undo of a rule run that
   232	 * settled the cursor's occurrence (`docs/specs/loan-installment-settlement.md`
   233	 * section 12.6): put the cursor columns back to `change.before`, but only
   234	 * while `next_due_date` still stands where that advance left it
   235	 * (`change.after`), so a cursor the person has moved since is left as they
   236	 * set it. Returns whether the cursor was rewound. When it was, the override
   237	 * rows the advance pruned are re-inserted, `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` so an
   238	 * override the person has since re-created for the same occurrence stands.
   239	 *
   240	 * Scoped to `userId`: an undo only ever touches the acting user's schedules.
   241	 */
   242	export async function rewindScheduleCursor(
   243	  m: EntityManager,
   244	  scheduleId: string,
   245	  userId: string,
   246	  change: ScheduleCursorChange,
   247	): Promise<boolean> {
   248	  const result = await m
   249	    .createQueryBuilder()
   250	    .update(ScheduledTransaction)
   251	    .set({
   252	      nextDueDate: change.before.nextDueDate,
   253	      occurrencesRemaining: change.before.occurrencesRemaining,
   254	      isActive: change.before.isActive,
   255	      lastPostedDate: change.before.lastPostedDate,
   256	    })
   257	    .where("id = :id", { id: scheduleId })
   258	    .andWhere("userId = :userId", { userId })
   259	    .andWhere("nextDueDate = :after", { after: change.after.nextDueDate })
   260	    .execute();
   261	  if ((result.affected ?? 0) === 0) return false;
   262	  if (change.prunedOverrides.length > 0) {
   263	    await m
   264	      .createQueryBuilder()
   265	      .insert()
   266	      .into(ScheduledTransactionOverride)
   267	      .values(
   268	        change.prunedOverrides.map((override) => ({
   269	          ...override,
   270	          scheduledTransactionId: scheduleId,
   271	        })),
   272	      )
   273	      .orIgnore()
   274	      .execute();
   275	  }
   276	  return true;
   277	}

# monize: issue drafts, round 2026-11-04-93f4e68-review

Second file-mode run on kenlasko/monize (control run, arm A run 2). Reviewed `main` at `93f4e685dc8b46e97adc8be2c7ed2ace766d7ee9`; today's `main` is `fbf01ab`, and none of the cited files changed between the two except `database/schema.sql`, which adds one more table that cascades on category delete (named in draft 3). Nothing here is filed: `gh` stayed read-only, and each draft waits for Garrett's written go (FILING.md section 8). The repo has no issue template, so the section 5 form is used as is. Four drafts; two findings held back under *Not filing*.

Before drafting, open and closed issues and pull requests were searched (`gh search issues` / `gh search prs`, 2026-11-04) for each finding: no match. Issue #1815 (closed 2026-10-22) fixed the strict reconciled lock being skipped on split-transfer and cross-owner edits of the *requested* row (its A26-M11); draft 1 is the next door along and cites it under Related.

---

## Draft 1

**Title:** [Bug] Voiding one leg of a transfer voids its reconciled counterpart in the other account, with "Lock reconciled transactions" on

**Version:** `main` at `93f4e68` (unchanged on today's `main`, `fbf01ab`).

**Summary:** The strict reconciled lock is asked of the row the request names and never of the rows the same write reaches. `applyStatusTransition` checks `[locked]` only (`backend/src/transactions/transaction-reconciliation.service.ts:130-135`), then `applyVoidTransitionToMirrorLeg` (`backend/src/transactions/void-status-transition.util.ts:125-144`) locks the counterpart leg, writes `status` on it and moves its account balance with no lock check. The generic row update does the same (`backend/src/transactions/transactions.service.ts:2813`, then `:3111`). The paired routes get it right: `removeTransfer` passes both legs to the check (`backend/src/transactions/transaction-transfer.service.ts:1606-1616`) and the bulk route expands to mirror legs before checking (`transaction-bulk-update.service.ts:1418-1470`, `:725`).

**Result:** with the lock on, voiding the unreconciled leg of a transfer sets the other account's RECONCILED leg to VOID (its `reconciled_date` stays), and that account's balance moves by the leg's amount. The account the user reconciled against a statement no longer matches it, and the row that should have been immovable was changed by a request that never named it.

**Where:** `backend/src/transactions/transaction-reconciliation.service.ts:130-135`, `:208-214`; `backend/src/transactions/void-status-transition.util.ts:125-144`; `backend/src/transactions/transactions.service.ts:2813`, `:3111`.

**Steps:**
1. Settings: turn on "Lock reconciled transactions".
2. Create a transfer of 100.00 from Chequing to Savings, dated last month.
3. In Savings, reconcile that leg (status cell to Reconciled; wait past the ten-second undo window).
4. Void the Chequing leg through the status route: `PATCH /transactions/<chequing leg id>/status` with `{"status":"VOID"}` (the register's status cell does not offer VOID, so the API, the MCP tools or the assistant are the doors; `PATCH /transactions/<id>` with `{"status":"VOID"}` is the same path).
5. Open Savings.

**Expected:** 409 "This transaction is reconciled and locked", as `DELETE /transactions/<id>/transfer` answers for the same pair; nothing written.

**Actual:** 200. The Savings leg is now VOID with its reconciled date still set, and Savings' balance is 100.00 lower than the statement it was reconciled to.

**How this was found:** an AI-assisted review of the source, confirmed by reading the code and running a small standalone program that copies the `applyStatusTransition`, `applyVoidTransitionToMirrorLeg` and `assertReconciledRowsMutable` logic. Not reproduced in the running app, so the steps above are what the code says will happen.

**Probe output** (`probe_void_mirror_leg.js`, scenario 1):
```
Scenario 1: strict lock ON, Savings leg RECONCILED; PATCH /transactions/legA/status {status: VOID}
  before
    legA (Chequing): status=CLEARED reconciledDate=null
    legB (Savings):  status=RECONCILED reconciledDate=2026-10-31
    balances: Chequing=900.00 Savings=1100.00
    DELETE /transactions/legA/transfer (both legs checked): 409 reconciledLockedError: This transaction is reconciled and locked.
    status route result: balanceMoved=true counterpartAccounts=["sav"] (no refusal)
  after
    legA (Chequing): status=VOID reconciledDate=null
    legB (Savings):  status=VOID reconciledDate=2026-10-31
    balances: Chequing=1000.00 Savings=1000.00
```

**Related:** the same cause on the split side: replacing or removing a split parent's lines checks the lock on the parent only (`transactions.service.ts:2813` then `:2895`; `transaction-split.service.ts:973`, `:1136`, `:1327`) and `deleteSplitSideEffects` / `removeLinkedLeg` then delete the transfer counterpart legs in other accounts (`transaction-split.service.ts:884-888`, `:1295`) whatever their status, so a reconciled counterpart leg is deleted outright. #1815 (A26-M11) closed the neighbouring gap where the *requested* row's lock was skipped.

**Possible fix:** in `applyVoidTransitionToMirrorLeg`, pass the locked counterpart through `assertReconciledRowsMutable` before writing (and refuse, not skip); in `deleteSplitSideEffects` do the same for the locked legs before `removeLockedTransactionLeg`. Test: lock on, counterpart RECONCILED, each of the three doors (status route, generic update, split rebuild) returns 409 and leaves both rows and both balances unchanged; `reconciled-lock.guard.spec.ts` could require every `removeLockedTransactionLeg` / mirror write to sit after an assertion over the same rows.

---

## Draft 2

**Title:** [Bug] Restoring a voided transfer leg to Reconciled marks the other account's leg Reconciled too, with no reconciled date

**Version:** `main` at `93f4e68` (unchanged on today's `main`, `fbf01ab`).

**Summary:** `updateStatus` resolves to whatever status the request carries (`backend/src/transactions/transaction-reconciliation.service.ts:240-242`), so VOID -> RECONCILED is accepted there although the dedicated `reconcile` route refuses it (`:273-282`). When the transition crosses the VOID boundary, `applyVoidTransitionToMirrorLeg` writes the *exact* new status onto the counterpart leg (`backend/src/transactions/void-status-transition.util.ts:136`), not merely the crossing. INV-TRANSFER-001 says reconciliation states are per ledger and only VOID inclusion is shared. The generic update has the same two steps (`transactions.service.ts:3030-3031`, `:3111`).

**Result:** the leg in the other account becomes RECONCILED without that account having been reconciled, with `reconciled_date` NULL; that account's next reconciliation starts from a "previously reconciled" figure that includes a row nobody reconciled, and with the strict lock on the row is frozen.

**Where:** `backend/src/transactions/transaction-reconciliation.service.ts:240-242`; `backend/src/transactions/void-status-transition.util.ts:136`; `backend/src/transactions/transactions.service.ts:3111`.

**Steps:**
1. Create a transfer of 100.00 from Chequing to Savings, then void it (both legs VOID).
2. `PATCH /transactions/<chequing leg id>/status` with `{"status":"RECONCILED"}` (also reachable as `PATCH /transactions/<id>` with `{"status":"RECONCILED"}`).
3. Open the Savings register and the Savings reconcile screen.

**Expected:** either a refusal, as `POST /transactions/<id>/reconcile` gives ("Cannot reconcile a void transaction"), or the Chequing leg reconciled and the Savings leg restored to its own unreconciled state.

**Actual:** both legs are RECONCILED; the Savings leg has no reconciled date and was never reconciled in Savings.

**How this was found:** an AI-assisted review of the source, confirmed by reading the code and running a small standalone program that copies the `applyStatusTransition` and `applyVoidTransitionToMirrorLeg` logic. Not reproduced in the running app, so the steps above are what the code says will happen.

**Probe output** (`probe_void_mirror_leg.js`, scenario 2):
```
Scenario 2: both legs VOID; PATCH /transactions/legA/status {status: RECONCILED}
  before
    legA (Chequing): status=VOID reconciledDate=null
    legB (Savings):  status=VOID reconciledDate=null
    balances: Chequing=1000.00 Savings=1000.00
    status route result: balanceMoved=true counterpartAccounts=["sav"]
  after
    legA (Chequing): status=RECONCILED reconciledDate=2026-11-04
    legB (Savings):  status=RECONCILED reconciledDate=null
    balances: Chequing=900.00 Savings=1100.00
```

**Related:** VOID -> CLEARED through the same route marks the counterpart CLEARED, the same mirroring at lower cost.

**Possible fix:** have `updateStatus` refuse VOID -> RECONCILED as `reconcile` does; in `applyVoidTransitionToMirrorLeg`, write the counterpart as UNRECONCILED when leaving VOID (keep VOID when entering it). Test: both legs VOID, status route to RECONCILED on one leg: refusal, or own leg RECONCILED with a date and the counterpart UNRECONCILED.

---

## Draft 3

**Title:** [Bug] Deleting a category deletes the payroll deduction rules that use it and leaves budget lines with no category

**Version:** `main` at `93f4e68`; today's `main` (`fbf01ab`) adds `loan_fees`, also `ON DELETE CASCADE` on `category_id`.

**Summary:** `CategoriesService.remove` refuses a delete only for subcategories and for references counted by `getTransactionCount` (transactions, splits, scheduled transactions, scheduled splits: `backend/src/categories/categories.service.ts:593-616`, `:654-697`). Nothing counts budget lines or payroll deduction rules, and the schema decides for them: `payroll_deduction_rules.category_id` is `ON DELETE CASCADE` (`database/schema.sql:3640`; `backend/src/payroll-deductions/entities/payroll-deduction-rule.entity.ts:65`), `budget_categories.category_id` and `budget_period_categories.category_id` are `ON DELETE SET NULL` (`database/schema.sql:2424`, `:2472`).

**Result:** a category with no transactions but a payroll deduction rule and a budget line can be deleted with no warning; the rule is gone and the budget line survives with no category (how such a line renders was not checked). The action-history entry records only the category.

**Where:** `backend/src/categories/categories.service.ts:593-616`, `:654-697`; `database/schema.sql:2424`, `:2472`, `:3640`.

**Steps:**
1. Create a category "Union dues" with no transactions.
2. Add a payroll deduction rule for it, and a budget line for it in a budget.
3. Delete the category from the Categories page.

**Expected:** a refusal naming the rule and the budget line, as a referencing transaction gets ("Cannot delete category with N referencing transaction(s)"), or a prompt to reassign.

**Actual:** the category is deleted; the payroll deduction rule is gone with it, and the budget line keeps its amount with no category.

**How this was found:** an AI-assisted review of the source, confirmed by reading the code. Not reproduced in the running app, so the steps above are what the code says will happen.

**Related:** `reassignTransactions` (`categories.service.ts:700-775`), the step the refusal points the user to, moves transactions, splits and scheduled items only, so neither the rule nor the budget line can be moved before the delete.

**Possible fix:** count payroll deduction rules, budget lines (and `loan_fees` on main) in the delete guard and refuse with their names, or reassign them in `reassignTransactions`. Test: a category referenced only by a payroll rule, then only by a budget line, is refused; after a reassign both point at the target.

---

## Draft 4

**Title:** [Bug] Reassigning a category fails with a database error once the user has more than 65,535 transactions

**Version:** `main` at `93f4e68` (unchanged on today's `main`, `fbf01ab`).

**Summary:** `reassignTransactions` selects every transaction id the user owns and passes the whole list as `IN (:...transactionIds)` to the split update (`backend/src/categories/categories.service.ts:723-739`), and does the same for scheduled transaction ids (`:751-766`). TypeORM expands a spread array into one bind parameter per element, and the PostgreSQL wire protocol carries the parameter count as a 16-bit integer, so a list over 65,535 ids cannot be bound: the driver reports a bind error and the request fails. The list is the user's entire ledger, not the rows that reference the category.

# Review of kenlasko/monize at 93f4e68

# Findings

## 1: Voiding one leg of a transfer voids its reconciled counterpart in the other account while "Lock reconciled transactions" is on
Severity: wrong-result
Where: backend/src/transactions/transaction-reconciliation.service.ts:130, backend/src/transactions/transaction-reconciliation.service.ts:208, backend/src/transactions/void-status-transition.util.ts:136, backend/src/transactions/transactions.service.ts:2813, backend/src/transactions/transactions.service.ts:3111, at 93f4e68
What the user loses: the account they reconciled against a bank statement no longer matches it: a row the lock promised was immovable is set to VOID (its reconciled date kept) and the account's balance moves by its amount, from a request that never named that row. On the split side the same gap deletes a reconciled counterpart leg outright (backend/src/transactions/transaction-split.service.ts:887, :1295, after a lock check on the parent only at :973, :1136, :1327).
Steps:
1. Settings: turn on "Lock reconciled transactions".
2. Create a transfer of 100.00 from Chequing to Savings, dated last month.
3. In Savings, reconcile that leg; wait past the ten-second undo window.
4. PATCH /transactions/<chequing leg id>/status with {"status":"VOID"} (or PATCH /transactions/<id> with the same body; the register's status cell does not offer VOID).
5. Open Savings.
Expected: 409 "This transaction is reconciled and locked", as DELETE /transactions/<id>/transfer answers for the same pair; nothing written.
Actual: 200; the Savings leg is VOID with its reconciled date still set, and Savings' balance is 100.00 below the statement it was reconciled to.
Evidence: probe
```
Scenario 1: strict lock ON, Savings leg RECONCILED; PATCH /transactions/legA/status {status: VOID}
  before
    legA (Chequing): status=CLEARED reconciledDate=null
    legB (Savings):  status=RECONCILED reconciledDate=2026-10-31
    balances: Chequing=900.00 Savings=1100.00
    DELETE /transactions/legA/transfer (both legs checked): 409 reconciledLockedError: This transaction is reconciled and locked.
    status route result: balanceMoved=true counterpartAccounts=["sav"] (no refusal)
  after
    legA (Chequing): status=VOID reconciledDate=null
    legB (Savings):  status=VOID reconciledDate=2026-10-31
    balances: Chequing=1000.00 Savings=1000.00
```

## 2: Restoring a voided transfer leg to Reconciled marks the other account's leg Reconciled too, with no reconciled date
Severity: wrong-result
Where: backend/src/transactions/transaction-reconciliation.service.ts:240, backend/src/transactions/void-status-transition.util.ts:136, backend/src/transactions/transactions.service.ts:3111, at 93f4e68
What the user loses: the other account shows a row as reconciled that nobody reconciled there, with no reconciled date; its next reconciliation starts from a "previously reconciled" figure that includes it, and with the lock on the row is frozen. The status route accepts VOID -> RECONCILED although the dedicated reconcile route refuses it, and the mirror write copies the exact new status rather than only the VOID crossing.
Steps:
1. Create a transfer of 100.00 from Chequing to Savings, then void it (both legs VOID).
2. PATCH /transactions/<chequing leg id>/status with {"status":"RECONCILED"} (or PATCH /transactions/<id> with the same body).
3. Open the Savings register and the Savings reconcile screen.
Expected: a refusal, as POST /transactions/<id>/reconcile gives ("Cannot reconcile a void transaction"), or the Chequing leg reconciled and the Savings leg back in its own unreconciled state.
Actual: both legs RECONCILED; the Savings leg has no reconciled date and was never reconciled in Savings.
Evidence: probe
```
Scenario 2: both legs VOID; PATCH /transactions/legA/status {status: RECONCILED}
  before
    legA (Chequing): status=VOID reconciledDate=null
    legB (Savings):  status=VOID reconciledDate=null
    balances: Chequing=1000.00 Savings=1000.00
    status route result: balanceMoved=true counterpartAccounts=["sav"]
  after
    legA (Chequing): status=RECONCILED reconciledDate=2026-11-04
    legB (Savings):  status=RECONCILED reconciledDate=null
    balances: Chequing=900.00 Savings=1100.00
```

## 3: Deleting a category deletes the payroll deduction rules that use it and leaves budget lines with no category
Severity: data-loss
Where: backend/src/categories/categories.service.ts:579, backend/src/categories/categories.service.ts:654, database/schema.sql:3640, database/schema.sql:2424, database/schema.sql:2472, backend/src/payroll-deductions/entities/payroll-deduction-rule.entity.ts:65, at 93f4e68
What the user loses: a payroll deduction rule they configured is deleted without warning (the foreign key cascades), and a budget line keeps its amount but loses its category (the foreign key sets it null). The delete guard counts only transactions, splits, scheduled transactions and scheduled splits, and the reassign step it points to moves only those. Today's main adds loan_fees, also cascading on category_id.
Steps:
1. Create a category with no transactions.
2. Add a payroll deduction rule for it, and a budget line for it in a budget.
3. Delete the category from the Categories page.
Expected: a refusal naming the rule and the budget line, as a referencing transaction gets, or a prompt to reassign them.
Actual: the category is deleted; the payroll deduction rule is gone with it; the budget line survives with no category.
Evidence: reading

## 4: Reassigning a category fails with a database error once the user has more than 65,535 transactions
Severity: crash
Where: backend/src/categories/categories.service.ts:723, backend/src/categories/categories.service.ts:738, backend/src/categories/categories.service.ts:751, at 93f4e68
What the user loses: with a long history (the README's own case is thirty years of Money data) they cannot reassign a category's transactions, and so cannot delete a category the guard says to reassign first. The method selects every transaction id the user owns and binds the whole list as one IN (...) parameter per id; the PostgreSQL protocol carries the parameter count in 16 bits, so a list over 65,535 ids cannot be bound and the request fails. The same shape, with the smaller scheduled-transaction list, is in getTransactionCount (:677-690).
Steps:
1. A user with more than 65,535 transactions.
2. Categories page: reassign any category's transactions to another (POST /categories/<id>/reassign).
Expected: the rows move and a count is returned.
Actual: 500; nothing moves (one transaction, rolled back).
Evidence: reading

## 5: "Twice a Month" steps to the 15th and month-end whatever the start date, so a bill on the 1st and 16th gets the wrong due dates
Severity: wrong-result
Where: backend/src/common/recurrence.ts:139, frontend/src/lib/frequency.ts:64, frontend/src/i18n/messages/en/scheduledTransactions.json:323, at 93f4e68
What the user loses: a scheduled item started on the 1st is next due on the 31st, then the 15th, and auto-posts on those days; the start day is never offered again. Steps:

2. Save and look at the next due dates (bills list, calendar).
Expected: the 1st and the 16th (or the two days the user chose).
Actual: the 31st, the 15th, the 28th, the 15th, ...
Evidence: probe

# Findings

## 1: Voiding one leg of a transfer voids its reconciled counterpart in the other account while "Lock reconciled transactions" is on
Severity: wrong-result
Where: backend/src/transactions/transaction-reconciliation.service.ts:130, backend/src/transactions/transaction-reconciliation.service.ts:208, backend/src/transactions/void-status-transition.util.ts:136, backend/src/transactions/transactions.service.ts:2813, backend/src/transactions/transactions.service.ts:3111, at 93f4e68
What the user loses: the account they reconciled against a bank statement no longer matches it: a row the lock promised was immovable is set to VOID (its reconciled date kept) and the account's balance moves by its amount, from a request that never named that row. On the split side the same gap deletes a reconciled counterpart leg outright (backend/src/transactions/transaction-split.service.ts:887, :1295, after a lock check on the parent only at :973, :1136, :1327).
Steps:
1. Settings: turn on "Lock reconciled transactions".
2. Create a transfer of 100.00 from Chequing to Savings, dated last month.
3. In Savings, reconcile that leg; wait past the ten-second undo window.
4. PATCH /transactions/<chequing leg id>/status with {"status":"VOID"} (or PATCH /transactions/<id> with the same body; the register's status cell does not offer VOID).
5. Open Savings.
Expected: 409 "This transaction is reconciled and locked", as DELETE /transactions/<id>/transfer answers for the same pair; nothing written.
Actual: 200; the Savings leg is VOID with its reconciled date still set, and Savings' balance is 100.00 below the statement it was reconciled to.
Evidence: probe

What the user loses: the other account shows a row as reconciled that nobody reconciled there, with no reconciled date; its next reconciliation starts from a "previously reconciled" figure that includes it, and with the lock on the row is frozen. The status route accepts VOID -> RECONCILED although the dedicated reconcile route refuses it, and the mirror write copies the exact new status rather than only the VOID crossing.
Steps:

## 3: Deleting a category deletes the payroll deduction rules that use it and leaves budget lines with no category
Severity: data-loss
Where: backend/src/categories/categories.service.ts:579, backend/src/categories/categories.service.ts:654, database/schema.sql:3640, database/schema.sql:2424, database/schema.sql:2472, backend/src/payroll-deductions/entities/payroll-deduction-rule.entity.ts:65, at 93f4e68

# monize, round 2026-11-04-93f4e68-review (file mode, control run 2)

**Commit:** `0aac33b2d61acbfd8dacb239bcaacc60caceb1a6` on `main` of Dev Instincts ("reviews/monize/: round 2026-11-04-93f4e68-review (file mode, control run 2): 5 findings, 4 drafts, 1 held"). Only `reviews/monize/` was added; `ledger/findings.jsonl` and `ledger/projects.json` untouched; `tools/stats.py` run (STATS.md unchanged). Lock taken at start, released as the last step. Nothing filed, commented or posted; `gh` read-only throughout. Nothing from the clone was installed, built or run.

Files (all under `<projects>\dev-instincts\`):
- `reviews\monize\2026-11-04-93f4e68-review-issues.md` (4 drafts in the §5 form + Not filing)
- `reviews\monize\2026-11-04-93f4e68-review-findings.md` (CONTROL.md §4 form, 5 findings, no ids/instincts/ledger words, repo-relative paths)
- `reviews\monize\2026-11-04-93f4e68-review\ledger-rows.jsonl` (MZ-L08..MZ-L12, every README field incl. smell; for the judge)
- `reviews\monize\2026-11-04-93f4e68-review\probes\` (2 probes, their outputs, the AGPL-3.0 LICENSE)
- `reviews\monize\2026-11-04-93f4e68-review.md` (the round report)

## Findings (reviewed sha 93f4e685dc8b46e97adc8be2c7ed2ace766d7ee9; today's main fbf01ab, cited files unchanged except schema.sql adding `loan_fees`)

| Id | Severity | file:line (at 93f4e68) | Evidence | Drafted |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MZ-L08 | wrong-result | backend/src/transactions/transaction-reconciliation.service.ts:130-135, :208-214; backend/src/transactions/void-status-transition.util.ts:125-144; backend/src/transactions/transactions.service.ts:2813, :3111; sibling: transaction-split.service.ts:884-888, :973, :1136, :1295, :1327 | probe (`probe_void_mirror_leg.js` scenario 1) | yes, draft 1 |
| MZ-L09 | wrong-result | transaction-reconciliation.service.ts:240-242; void-status-transition.util.ts:136; transactions.service.ts:3016-3017, :3111 | probe (scenario 2) | yes, draft 2 |
| MZ-L10 | data-loss | backend/src/categories/categories.service.ts:582-616, :654-697, :700-775; database/schema.sql:2424, :2472, :3640; backend/src/payroll-deductions/entities/payroll-deduction-rule.entity.ts:65 | reading | yes, draft 3 |
| MZ-L11 | crash | categories.service.ts:723-739, :751-766 (same shape :674-690) | reading | yes, draft 4 |
| MZ-L12 | wrong-result | backend/src/common/recurrence.ts:139-148; frontend/src/lib/frequency.ts:64-73; frontend/src/i18n/messages/en/scheduledTransactions.json:323 | probe (`probe_semimonthly_step.js`) | no (both implementations and tests agree; likely design hidden by the "Twice a Month" label; Garrett decides) |

In one line each:
- **MZ-L08**: with "Lock reconciled transactions" on, voiding one transfer leg via `PATCH /transactions/:id/status` or `PATCH /transactions/:id` sets the other account's RECONCILED leg to VOID (reconciled date kept) and moves that balance; the lock is checked on the requested row only, while `removeTransfer` and the bulk route check both legs and refuse. Same cause: split rebuild/removal deletes reconciled counterpart legs. Probe: paired delete 409, status route "no refusal", Savings leg VOID, balance moved 100.00.
- **MZ-L09**: `updateStatus` accepts VOID -> RECONCILED (the `reconcile` route refuses it) and the mirror helper copies the exact new status, so the other account's leg becomes RECONCILED with reconciledDate null, never reconciled there (contradicts INV-TRANSFER-001).
- **MZ-L10**: category delete guard counts transactions/splits/scheduled only; `payroll_deduction_rules.category_id` is ON DELETE CASCADE (rule silently deleted), budget line category_ids SET NULL; reassign moves none of them. Main adds `loan_fees` (also CASCADE).
